prompt: Which question separates the three ways of deploying a model?

choices.text: The age of an answer when somebody reads it
choices.why: Right. A night, a request's features, or the model on the device.

choices.text: Which language the model was trained in
choices.why: All three serve the same scikit-learn model here.

choices.text: How many members the shop has in total
choices.why: Batch scores thousands and a service one, but size does not decide it.

choices.text: Whether the model came from MLflow or from DVC
choices.why: Every place loads the same registered champion.

prompt: Marketing sends vouchers once a month from a list of likely lapsers. Where should the lapse model run?

choices.text: In a web service called for each member
choices.why: A score from last night is as good for a monthly list, and far cheaper.

choices.text: In a batch, on a schedule
choices.why: Right. A decision taken on a schedule is served by scores computed on one.

choices.text: On each member's phone
choices.why: Nothing about the decision needs the device.

choices.text: Inside the voucher e-mail itself
choices.why: An e-mail runs no model.

prompt: Which of these call for real-time scoring rather than a nightly batch? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: A fraud check on a payment made a second ago
choices.why: Right. The payment did not exist last night.

choices.text: A recommendation that changes when a book goes in the basket
choices.why: Right. The answer depends on what just happened.

choices.text: The monthly list of members to send a voucher
choices.why: A list made monthly is a batch.

choices.text: A dashboard of last quarter's lapse rate
choices.why: That is a report on the past, not a prediction per request.

prompt: How does score_batch.py know which model version to load?

choices.text: It loads the newest version registered
choices.why: Newest is not champion: version 2 is newer and is not used.

choices.text: The version is passed on the command line
choices.why: Only the cutoff is.

choices.text: It reads the champion alias
choices.why: Right. Then it loads that number and records it on every row.

choices.text: It trains a fresh model every night
choices.why: It trains nothing; it scores with a registered model.

prompt: score_batch.py is asked for a night the feature store has no snapshot of. What does it do?

choices.text: Scores with the most recent snapshot
choices.why: That would label old features with tonight's date.

choices.text: Computes the features from shop.db
choices.why: That would be a second implementation, the skew lesson 5 warned about.

choices.text: Writes a row of zeros for each member
choices.why: A zero is a score, and a wrong one.

choices.text: Refuses, naming the date
choices.why: Right. A night with no snapshot is not scored from whatever is lying around.

prompt: What does each row of lapse_scores carry? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: the member's id
choices.why: Right. Half of the key.

choices.text: the cutoff the score is as of
choices.why: Right. The other half.

choices.text: the model version
choices.why: Right. A report mixing two versions can tell them apart.

choices.text: whether the member then lapsed
choices.why: Nobody knows that for 90 days; lesson 9 joins it later.

prompt: How many members did the batch score as of 28 February 2026?
Why does score_batch.py delete the night's rows before inserting them?

choices.text: So that a rerun replaces the night instead of doubling it
choices.why: Right. Appending would count every member twice, with no error anywhere.

choices.text: To free disk space between runs
choices.why: It deletes one night and writes the same night back.

choices.text: SQLite has no UPDATE statement
choices.why: It has one; delete and insert is simply clearer for a whole night.

choices.text: Old scores are confidential
choices.why: Other nights are kept on purpose.

prompt: A step that leaves the same result however many times it runs is called ___.
Why are last month's scores kept instead of being overwritten by this month's?

choices.text: SQLite cannot overwrite a primary key
choices.why: It can; the job does that for a rerun of the same night.

choices.text: Old scores against what members then did grade the model
choices.why: Right. Lesson 9 needs the scores of 28 February next to the 90 days after it.

choices.text: Marketing compares this month's list with last month's
choices.why: Maybe, but that is not the reason the lesson gives.

choices.text: The law requires every score to be kept for five years
choices.why: No law is involved here.

prompt: Match each library to its job in this lesson.
Why does serve.py load the model outside the request function?

choices.text: FastAPI forbids imports inside a function
choices.why: It forbids nothing of the kind.

choices.text: The model changes on every request
choices.why: It is pinned for the life of the process.

choices.text: Loading once keeps each request to a lookup and a prediction
choices.why: Right. What can be done once is done at start-up.

choices.text: MLflow allows one load per day
choices.why: No such limit exists.

prompt: The champion alias moves from version 1 to version 2 while serve.py is running. What does the service answer with?

choices.text: Version 2, from the next request on
choices.why: It read the alias once, at start-up.

choices.text: A mix of both, request by request
choices.why: Pinning at start-up is exactly what prevents that.

choices.text: An error until somebody reloads it
choices.why: The loaded model keeps working.

choices.text: Version 1, until it restarts
choices.why: Right. And every response says which version answered.

prompt: Where do the service's features come from?

choices.text: The online store, through get
choices.why: Right. Never computed in the service, so skew is kept out by construction.

choices.text: features.py, run on the request
choices.why: That would query 180 days of purchases per request.

choices.text: The request body, sent by the caller
choices.why: The request carries only the member id.

choices.text: A CSV loaded at start-up
choices.why: A CSV is what edge.py reads.

prompt: The service answers 404 for member 8. Why?

choices.text: Member 8 does not exist in the shop
choices.why: They exist; their features are what is missing.

choices.text: The online store left them out as too old
choices.why: Right. The service refuses rather than inventing a score.

choices.text: The service crashed on that request
choices.why: A crash would be a 500, not a reason in the body.

choices.text: The URL was typed wrong
choices.why: It is the same route as member 2's.

prompt: A request for /lapse/abc gets a 422. Which part of the system answered it?

choices.text: The model, which cannot score letters
choices.why: The request never reached the model.

choices.text: The online store, which has no member abc
choices.why: The store was never asked.

choices.text: FastAPI, checking the declared type
choices.why: Right. member_id: int; the function never ran.

choices.text: curl, before sending the request
choices.why: curl sends anything; the body came from the server.

prompt: Lesson 7 printed 0.090 for member 2; the service says 0.098. What explains it?

choices.text: The service uses version 2
choices.why: The response says model_version 1.

choices.text: Rounding to three places differs
choices.why: 0.008 is far beyond rounding.

choices.text: One of them has a bug
choices.why: Both are right for their dates.

choices.text: The two score different dates
choices.why: Right. 30 November against tonight's snapshot: a score is always as of something.

prompt: Why is the model exported to ONNX for the device instead of loaded through MLflow?

choices.text: There is no room there for a gigabyte of libraries
choices.why: Right. ONNX plus a small runtime is what fits there.

choices.text: ONNX models are more accurate
choices.why: The probabilities came out identical.

choices.text: MLflow cannot load a pipeline
choices.why: The batch and the service load one through it.

choices.text: ONNX is required by the registry
choices.why: The registry holds the scikit-learn pipeline.

prompt: How many bytes was the exported lapse-v1.onnx?
What does the lesson check before an ONNX file is shipped?

choices.text: That the file is under two kilobytes
choices.why: Size was a result, not the check.

choices.text: Same rows, same scores both ways
choices.why: Right. A converter that handles a step differently is skew moved onto a device.

choices.text: That onnxruntime is newer than scikit-learn
choices.why: Version numbers say nothing about the answers.

choices.text: That the device has a network connection
choices.why: The point of the edge is not needing one.

prompt: Which problems does running the model on the device make harder? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: computing the features
choices.why: Right. A second implementation, on hardware you cannot reach.

choices.text: updating the version
choices.why: Right. Several versions answer at once for months.

choices.text: keeping the evidence
choices.why: Right. Answers stay on the device unless it sends them back.

choices.text: the size of the model file
choices.why: 1,803 bytes is not the problem.

prompt: Why can many of the lapse model's features not be computed on a till?

choices.text: Tills cannot run Python
choices.why: ONNX needs no Python; the data is the problem.

choices.text: ONNX forbids string inputs
choices.why: The export declared three string inputs.

choices.text: A till knows today's purchase, not 180 days of a member
choices.why: Right. And a model that needs them cannot go there.

choices.text: The features are encrypted
choices.why: Nothing here is encrypted.

prompt: Why does canary.py choose the group with a hash of the member id, not a random draw per request?

choices.text: A hash is faster than a random number
choices.why: Speed is not the point.

choices.text: Random numbers are not allowed in production
choices.why: They are; per request they would split one person.

choices.text: So the canary gets the members likeliest to lapse
choices.why: That would be choosing who is in it, the thing it must not do.

choices.text: Same member, same group, chosen by nobody
choices.why: Right. The two rules that make a canary trustworthy.

prompt: What share of the canary's members did version 2 put over 0.2? Answer as a percentage.
The canary caught version 2 without waiting for any labels. What did it compare?

choices.text: What each version said
choices.why: Right. 0.421 against 0.175 on members drawn alike: the difference is the model's.

choices.text: Each group's accuracy
choices.why: Accuracy needs outcomes, which take 90 days.

choices.text: Each version's response time
choices.why: It ran no service; it compared scores.

choices.text: The size of each model file
choices.why: File size says nothing about scores.

prompt: A deployment where the new version scores every request but its answers are only logged is called a ___ deployment.
The member page wants a lapse score. What does the lesson recommend?

choices.text: A real-time service, since a page is live
choices.why: It would answer what last night's row says, with an outage risk.

choices.text: Reading last night's row from lapse_scores
choices.why: Right. The score cannot be fresher than its features, which change when a member buys.

choices.text: Running the ONNX file in the browser
choices.why: The browser has none of the features.

choices.text: Retraining the model when the page opens
choices.why: Training per page view is never the answer.

prompt: Match each deployment to what it looks like when it fails.

pairs.right: a stale table until tomorrow's run

right_distractors: a model that trains itself again

prompt: Put the steps of a careful move from version 1 to version 2 in order.
items: send one member in ten to it
compare what the two groups were told
move the alias, or stop the canary

prompt: A team builds a real-time service for a model whose inputs change once a night. What have they bought?

choices.text: Fresher scores than any batch could give
choices.why: The score cannot be fresher than its features.

choices.text: A model that needs no monitoring
choices.why: A service needs more monitoring, not less.

choices.text: Last night's answer, with an outage risk
choices.why: Right. The table never had that risk.

choices.text: Better calibrated probabilities
choices.why: Where a model runs does not change what it says.
